newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian exchange sees new listing system in May.
newsitem.headline: Russian exchange sees new listing system in May.

text.p: The Russian Trading System, Russia's main equities market, could be ready to introduce a new listing system reflecting disclosure levels by companies in May, a senior exchange official said on Wednesday.

"I think that very soon, perhaps as early as the beginning of May, we will order companies according to the requirements of the quote lists," Dmitry Ponomarev, President of the national brokers association NAUFOR which runs the RTS, told a news conference.

According to rules set out by the Federal Commission on the Securities Market, shares traded on the RTS system would also appear on officially recognised level-one and level-two quote lists, a NAUFOR spokesman told Reuters.

Conditions for inclusion in the new level-one quote list include the requirement that the company filing the shares is also the issuer and that it provides any information requested by the RTS under Securities Commission rules.
"This allows, firstly, a more transparent market," said the spokesman.

Ponomarev said four Russian stocks, retailers GUM and TsUM, regional telecoms company Uralsvyazinform and oil production unit Chernogorneft are ready to be added to the new RTS level-one quote listing.
"There are 10 more stocks which are on their way there," Ponomarev said.
The NAUFOR spokesman said the new rules applied to other organisations and exchanges which organise stock trading.
RTS already operates two segments for shares. Leading shares are traded on the main RTS system, and less liquid stocks on the new RTS-2 market.
The RTS also announced on Wednesday that as of Thursday, prices quoted by information vendors such as Reuters would appear with only a three-minute delay instead of a 10-minute delay as previously.
